summarise.explanation: Join typed tables through a declared foreign key, optionally filter integers, then group and count/sum exact integer amounts. Choose this for reproducible relational reports and a fresh checked database. Null join keys are omitted, null values are ignored by SUM, and an all-null group has a null total.
pitfalls: Use exact JSON integers, explicit nullability and primary/foreign keys; do not pass SQL or a pre-existing database.

fields.explanation: Declare the complete relational report, from captured typed source tables to ordered groups. Each execution creates a new database; changing source bytes requires a new run.

/properties/version.explanation: Select the SQLite document contract schemaxis.sqlite/1. This version names the input language; the qualified native release is recorded separately.

/properties/operation.explanation: Join typed tables through a declared foreign key, optionally filter integers, then group and count/sum exact integer amounts. Choose this for reproducible relational reports and a fresh checked database. Null join keys are omitted, null values are ignored by SUM, and an all-null group has a null total.

/properties/tables.explanation: Declare parent tables before children so foreign keys can name an earlier primary key. Every source is captured before native execution; 1–4 tables and up to 2048 rows each are supported.

/properties/tables/items.explanation: Describe one imported table and its ownership: a local JSON array of exact row objects, declared column types, primary key and optional foreign keys. Empty arrays are valid.

/properties/tables/items/properties/name.explanation: Give this table a unique lower-case ASCII identifier, such as sales. Qualified query fields use this name; SQLite internal names are excluded.

/properties/tables/items/properties/sour.explanation: Choose an absolute regular local .json row-array file. Rows must contain exactly the declared columns, with actual JSON nulls where allowed; file symlinks and duplicate JSON keys are rejected. Workflow reuse hashes the captured bytes.

/properties/tables/items/properties/colu.explanation: List every source column in database order. Choose INTEGER for exact unitless integer arithmetic or TEXT for printable ASCII labels; automatic conversion is forbidden.
Describe one typed column. Nullability is explicit and defaults to false; a primary-key column must remain nonnullable.
Name the source object key with a distinct lower-case ASCII identifier. Case and spelling must match each source row exactly.
Choose INTEGER for actual JSON integers within ±1000000000 (booleans excluded), or TEXT for up to 256 printable ASCII characters. No float parsing, date interpretation or unit conversion occurs.
Allow actual JSON null in this column when true. Omission forbids null; empty text and zero are values, never missing data. Primary-key columns cannot allow null.

/properties/tables/items/properties/prim.explanation: Choose a nonnullable column whose values uniquely identify all rows. Duplicate primary values fail before native execution; this key is the only allowed foreign-key target.

/properties/tables/items/properties/fore.explanation: Declare at most four parent relationships. Omission means no foreign keys; every nonnull local value must exist in the earlier parent table, even if a later query would filter that row out.
Connect a child column to an earlier table primary key of the same type. Null local keys are allowed only when the column is nullable and do not match an inner join.
Name the child column carrying the parent identity. Use one foreign-key relationship per local column, and declare its nullability deliberately.
Name an earlier declared parent table. Tables cannot reference themselves or later imports in this bounded contract.
Name the earlier parent table primaryKey column. A same-type unique primary key prevents accidental many-to-many row expansion.

/properties/from.explanation: Choose the base table supplying report rows. Without join, all query columns must belong to this table; with join, both base and parent columns are available.

/properties/join.explanation: Optionally enrich base rows with one parent table by following a declared foreign key. Omission keeps base rows alone; inner join drops null local keys and cannot multiply rows through a duplicate parent.

/properties/join/properties/table.explanation: Choose the earlier parent table named by a base-table foreign key. This is an inner join only; unmatched nonnull keys are an input integrity error.

/properties/join/properties/local.explanation: Name the base-table foreign-key column used to find its parent. Null local keys produce no joined row.

/properties/join/properties/remote.explanation: Name the joined parent primary key, matching the base foreign-key declaration exactly. Composite and non-key joins are excluded.

/properties/where.explanation: Optionally keep only rows whose chosen INTEGER column is at least minimum, after joining. Omission keeps all joined rows; null filtered values do not pass.

/properties/where/properties/column.explanation: Choose a qualified INTEGER field such as sales.id or sales.amount from the active tables. Null values fail this filter; text comparison and expressions are excluded.

/properties/where/properties/minimum.explanation: Set an inclusive exact integer threshold in the same units as the selected column; no units are inferred. For example 3 keeps IDs 3 and above. The threshold must remain within ±1000000000.

/properties/groupBy.explanation: Choose 1–3 distinct qualified columns defining groups. Output names g0, g1 and g2 follow this order; binary ascending ordering places null first and distinguishes null, empty string, zero and text case.

/properties/groupBy/items.explanation: Name one active table.column, such as departments.region. All rows with identical typed values form one group; no case folding or numeric/text coercion occurs.

/properties/sum.explanation: Choose a qualified INTEGER amount column to sum after joining/filtering. Null amounts are ignored; all-null groups produce null totals. row_count still includes those rows. Empty query results publish headers with zero rows.
